description: The Debug workspace answers the scripted transport replays (windows/App.Core/Testing/ScriptedDaemon.Debug.cs). operations/list: the Windows daemon's operation.describe and operation.list answers for the six Debug operations, availability set to available; probe: debug-probe probe.full; plan: deploy-native-library deployed.plan; runs: the recorded job.run answers (debug.template@1 reuses capture.diagnostics@1's shape). Generated by the TASK-XPA-020 Debug slice from rust/tests/fixtures.

inputs.description: Optional ability identity carried into the liveness artifact; never lowered as caller-supplied argv.
inputs.name: abilityName

inputs.description: Capture ArkUI componentDetail output for one selected component. Requires the typed windowId and componentId inputs; absent or false leaves the plan unchanged.
inputs.name: advancedDump

inputs.description: Optional typed application identity. When present, the same bounded job publishes an application-specific process readback.
inputs.name: bundleName

inputs.description: Capture the bounded HiLog artifact. Set false for a typed UI snapshot that needs the component tree and PNG but not diagnostic logs.
inputs.name: captureHilog

inputs.description: Validated ArkUI accessibility/component identifier used only by the componentDetail recipe.
inputs.name: componentId

inputs.description: One Faultlogger entry to fetch, named exactly as the index lists it. An entry name, never a path.
inputs.name: crashLogName

inputs.description: Capture the device's Faultlogger index. Read-only: unlike the trace, tree and screenshot legs this does not raise the effective effect.
inputs.name: crashLogs

inputs.description: Bounded HiLog capture window.
inputs.name: durationSeconds

inputs.description: Caller-supplied expected digest of the deployment whose liveness is being sampled. Recorded with the observation so a later reader can tell which build was live; it is not trusted as a fact about the device.
inputs.name: expectedDeployedArtifactDigest

inputs.description: Typed HiLog filter expressions; no shell fragments.
inputs.name: hilogFilters

inputs.description: Host-side marks collected during the captured window, each an RFC 3339 instant with an optional `#label`. They reach no device: a mark is an annotation on host time, and the capture only carries it into `markers.json` so a reader can line it up with what the device recorded.
inputs.name: markers

inputs.description: Optional process identity. Defaults to bundleName and is lowered only by the HDC provider.
inputs.name: processName

inputs.description: Redaction applied to published text. This field is retained as a forward-compatible policy dimension, but currently has one executable value: `standard`. Stronger redaction is not published until its implementation exists.
inputs.name: redactionProfile

inputs.description: Arm the trace ring, let the window pass, then snapshot it, instead of blocking for the window with `-t N`. The snapshot carries everything since the arm, bounded by the buffer, so the decision to keep a trace can be made after the thing worth keeping rather than before it. Only consulted when traceCategories selects the trace leg.
inputs.name: ringBuffered

inputs.description: Encoding for the screenshot leg. PNG is the evidence format and stays the default; JPEG is measurably cheaper - p50 638 ms against 858 ms and 40,947 bytes against 448,352, over 50 captures each on 2026-08-26 - and is for work that wants a current picture rather than a record. The device validates the file suffix against this, so the type and the owned path are one decision.
inputs.name: screenshotImageType

inputs.description: Ceiling on the total bytes this job may publish across all of its artifacts. Reaching it ends collection rather than silently dropping a product.
inputs.name: totalArtifactByteBudget

inputs.description: Per-capture trace buffer size in KiB. Only consulted when traceCategories selects the trace leg; ignored otherwise.
inputs.name: traceBufferKB

inputs.description: Trace categories; presence selects the remote-file trace leg and escalates the effective effect to deviceMutation.
inputs.name: traceCategories

inputs.description: Capture the on-screen component tree. Presence selects the file-producing dumpLayout leg and escalates the effective effect to deviceMutation; absent or false leaves the plan unchanged.
inputs.name: uiComponentTree

inputs.description: Capture the accessibility/window dump. Read-only: unlike the trace, screenshot and component-tree legs this does not raise the effective effect.
inputs.name: uiDump

inputs.description: Capture a PNG screenshot of the display. Presence selects the file-producing snapshot_display leg and escalates the effective effect to deviceMutation; absent or false leaves the plan unchanged.
inputs.name: uiScreenshot

inputs.description: Validated ArkUI host window identifier used only by the componentDetail recipe.
inputs.name: windowId

capture.diagnostics@1.title: Capture bounded HiLog, UI dump and trace with a structured artifact index

inputs.description: Ability to start within the bundle, as declared in module.json5, for example `EntryAbility`. Never lowered as caller-supplied argv.
inputs.name: abilityName

inputs.description: Feature HAPs and HSPs of the same bundle. Present means the packages are sent into one provider-owned directory and installed by a single bm install -p <dir>; absent leaves the single-package plan unchanged.
inputs.name: additionalHapArtifactLeases

inputs.description: Application bundle name exactly as the package declares it, for example `com.example.waterflow`. The provider matches package readback against this, so a bundle that is not installed by this exact name reads as a failed install.
inputs.name: bundleName

inputs.description: Collect the bounded HiLog window while the ability runs. Read-only, and its absence does not fail the job — the diagnostics artifact is optional.
inputs.name: captureDiagnostics

inputs.description: What happens to the package when the job ends. `uninstall` removes it; `retain` leaves it installed, which an external observer needs together with postRunAbilityState `running` to keep watching after the job succeeds. Restoring a previous package is not published until a snapshot/restore plan exists.
inputs.name: cleanupPolicy

inputs.description: Length of the bounded HiLog window in seconds. A crash that happens after this window is not in the artifact, so a delayed fault needs a window that outlasts it.
inputs.name: diagnosticsDurationSeconds

inputs.description: Entry HAP; must come from an artifact lease, arbitrary local paths are rejected.
inputs.name: hapArtifactLease

inputs.description: How an already-installed package is treated. This field is retained as a forward-compatible policy dimension, but currently has one executable value: `installOrReplace`. A fresh-only install is not published until a pre-install absence readback exists.
inputs.name: installPolicy

inputs.description: Port forwarding to establish alongside the run. This field is retained as a forward-compatible policy dimension, but currently has one executable value: `none`. This operation publishes no port-forward steps; use `port-forward.create@1` separately.
inputs.name: portForwardProfile

inputs.description: Whether the started ability is stopped before cleanup. `running` skips stop-ability so the application is still live when the job succeeds, which is what an external observer needs; the operator then owns stopping it. A failed job still stops the ability during compensation.
inputs.name: postRunAbilityState

debug.hap@1.title: Install, start, observe, stop and optionally uninstall a HAP from an artifact lease

inputs.description: Which closed read-only template to run. The remote command tokens, output budget and title of each member are provider-owned; the caller selects an identity and never supplies command text. `arkdeck debug template list` publishes the set with its disclosures.
inputs.name: templateId

debug.template@1.title: Run one approved read-only Debug command template on the bound device

inputs.description: ABI the uploaded ELF must declare. Verified against the artifact's own header before anything is sent, so a mismatch fails on the host rather than on the device.
inputs.name: expectedABI

inputs.description: The .so must come from an artifact lease; arbitrary local paths are rejected.
inputs.name: libraryArtifactLease

inputs.description: File name the library is published under inside the application's own directory. Must match `lib<name>.so` and be at most 128 characters; it names a file, never a path.
inputs.name: libraryLogicalName

inputs.description: How the application is restarted so it loads the new library. This field is retained as a forward-compatible policy dimension, but currently has one executable value: `restartAbility`. Other restart modes are not published until they have complete restart/readback plans.
inputs.name: restartProfile

inputs.description: What happens to the previous library when verification fails. `autoRollback` restores it; `retainBackup` leaves the new one in place and keeps the backup for a later decision.
inputs.name: rollbackPolicy

inputs.description: Remote destination is derived from this bundle's app-owned profile directory; callers cannot submit a remote path.
inputs.name: targetBundle

inputs.description: How much of the deployment is proven after publication. `hashOnly` compares the published bytes, `hashAndProcess` also requires the process to be live, and the default `hashProcessAndMaps` additionally requires the library to appear in the process's loaded maps.
inputs.name: verificationProfile

inputs.description: Which way the rule points. `forward` lowers to hdc `fport` — a host port reaching a device port; `reverse` lowers to `rport` — a device port reaching a host port.
inputs.name: direction

inputs.description: Port on the host side of the rule. Unprivileged range only.
inputs.name: localPort

inputs.description: Port on the device side of the rule. Unprivileged range only.
inputs.name: remotePort

inputs.description: Which rule to remove; must match the direction the rule was created with. `forward` is hdc `fport`, `reverse` is `rport`.
inputs.name: direction

inputs.description: Host-side port of the rule to remove; must match the rule exactly.
inputs.name: localPort

inputs.description: Device-side port of the rule to remove; must match the rule exactly.
inputs.name: remotePort
